title: An empirical attempt to identify binge gambling utilizing account-based player tracking data
tldr: K-means clustering of 150,895 British online gamblers identified two clusters with low gambling days but high intensity that may represent binge gambling, with 29% of one such cluster becoming inactive in subsequent months.
problem_and_motivation: Binge gambling is an under-explored construct with only self-report evidence from surveys and interviews. No prior study has used account-based player tracking data to operationalize or detect binge gambling. The episodic nature of binge gambling means it could evade existing detection algorithms used by online operators.
approach: Secondary anonymized dataset from a British online casino operator comprising 150,895 online gamblers with January-June 2023 data.
Fourteen player tracking variables plus age and gender were computed for each gambler over January-March 2023.
Min-max standardization was applied to the 14 behavioral features to equalize variable influence on cluster formation.
K-means cluster analysis was performed using Python and the sklearn package; the number of clusters was guided by scree plots and silhouette scores.
A six-cluster solution was selected based on cluster size, uniqueness, interpretability, and silhouette score of 0.44.
The cluster model was applied to April-June 2023 data to assess temporal stability of cluster memberships.
Median and 90th percentile analyses were conducted to examine distributional skew within clusters.
findings: num: 150,895 British online gamblers were analyzed, average age 39, 46% female.
num: Six clusters were identified; Clusters 2 (15%) and 5 (8%) exhibited low gambling days but high intensity consistent with binge gambling.
num: Cluster 2 averaged £1,021.08 bet per day and £85.91 deposited per day, highest of any cluster.
num: Cluster 5 had a median of 1 gambling day but 90th percentile of 32 sessions, indicating a small subgroup of extreme gamblers.
num: 29% of Cluster 5 gamblers and 17% of Cluster 2 gamblers stopped gambling entirely in April-June 2023.
num: Cluster 1 showed the highest retention at 70% remaining in the same cluster across periods.
num: 17% of all 150,895 players became inactive between April and June 2023.
num: Silhouette score for the six-cluster solution was 0.44.

key_equations.explanation: Min-max standardization rescales each variable to range [0,1] for equal clustering influence.
Silhouette score measures how similar a point is to its cluster vs. nearest cluster.

definitions.definition: Episodic gambling characterized by sudden onset of intense, time-limited gambling with acute harmful consequences and absence of gambling urges between episodes.
Unsupervised algorithm that partitions data into k clusters by minimizing within-cluster sum of squares.
Metric ranging from -1 to +1 measuring cluster cohesion and separation; higher values indicate better-defined clusters.
Plot of within-cluster sum of squares versus number of clusters used to identify the optimal cluster count via the elbow method.
Account-based behavioral records of individual gambling transactions including bets, deposits, wins, and withdrawals.
Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th edition, which reclassified gambling disorder as a behavioral addiction.
International Classification of Diseases, 11th revision, which describes gambling disorder as persistent and recurrent maladaptive gambling.
Rescaling procedure that transforms each variable to a 0-1 range by subtracting the minimum and dividing by the range.
Less than five pounds remaining in a gambling account at the end of a session, used as an indicator of potential chasing behavior.
Mechanism allowing gamblers to voluntarily block themselves from gambling platforms.
Continuing to gamble after losses, often characterized by increased deposits and session deposits.
Binge Gambling Screening Tool, a nine-item instrument developed by Cowlishaw et al. to identify binge gambling in clinical settings.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides the first empirical attempt to identify binge gambling using account-based player tracking data rather than self-report methods.
directly_justifies: Two clusters gambled on relatively low days but displayed high gambling intensity, matching binge gambling profiles.
29% of Cluster 5 gamblers and 17% of Cluster 2 gamblers stopped gambling entirely in the following three months.
Cluster 2 averaged £1,021.08 bet per day and Cluster 5 averaged £827.48, both higher than any other cluster.
Silhouette score for the six-cluster solution was 0.44.
17% of all 150,895 players became inactive between April and June 2023.
limits: Data from a single British online casino operator may not represent the totality of an individual's gambling behavior.
Binge gambling may not be fully visible over the six-month observation window studied.
Shared accounts could confound individual behavior attribution.
No validated definition of binge gambling frequency or intensity thresholds exists.
Cluster 5 heterogeneity suggests a small extreme subgroup drives average values within that cluster.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 5 was flagged as medium relevance because clustering methodology for gambling behavioral profiles is transferable to financial behavioral profiling. Domain 8 received medium relevance since the paper treats binge gambling clusters as outliers identifiable through unsupervised methods. Domain 12 received low relevance for evaluation methodology.

limitations: Data from a single UK online casino operator means results may not generalize to other operators or offline gambling.
Six-month observation window may be insufficient to capture the full episodic cycle of binge gambling.
Shared accounts could confound individual behavioral attribution.
The six-cluster solution silhouette score of 0.44 indicates moderate rather than strong cluster homogeneity.
No validated operational definition of binge gambling thresholds for frequency or intensity exists.
Binge gambling clusters did not show high rates of account depletion or frequent depositing, contradicting some theoretical expectations.
remember_this: K-means clustering of 150,895 British online gamblers revealed six distinct behavioral profiles from 14 tracking variables.
Two clusters showed low gambling days but high monetary intensity, potentially matching binge gambling patterns.
Cluster 2 bet an average of £1,021.08 per day, highest across all clusters, on only about 10 playing days.
29% of Cluster 5 gamblers and 17% of Cluster 2 gamblers stopped gambling entirely in the following three months.
The episodic nature of binge gambling may cause it to evade continuous monitoring algorithms used by operators.
